lessons: Expert MAJOR deferred: senior / disability / small-business discounts are named but never quantified (no age threshold for azrach vatik, no discount magnitude, no legal basis, no application mechanism). Next cycle: source each entitlement from the BoI fee rules and add a discounts table plus a calculator flag.

Expert MAJOR deferred: population-based exemptions absent (soldiers in sadir, students, young account holders). For those cohorts these are worth more than any track switch, and the skill's own problem statement promises 'discounts for eligible populations'.

Expert MAJOR deferred: no path to recover money already charged. Missing that account closure must be free and cannot be blocked, that a fee charged contrary to the rules or the tariff is refundable retroactively on complaint, and that a debit taken without consent or above the agreed ceiling can be reclaimed from the bank. Section B stops at stopping future payments.

Expert MAJOR deferred: Template 2 (stop a debit authorization) will likely bounce at a real bank. Banks match a harshaa on beneficiary institution code plus authorization asmachta, not a free-text business name, and most require their own site or branch form rather than a letter. Next cycle: make the authorization ID mandatory, add a beneficiary-code + last-debit-date + amount fallback, and warn the letter may be refused in favour of the bank's channel.

Expert MINOR deferred: templates carry no reply-to block or response deadline; Template 1 does not warn that issuers usually require an authenticated channel and that charges already incurred remain payable after cancellation; HE Troubleshooting omits the BoI escalation that EN includes.
